Maya Chen: quick heads-up — dropping a compact preflight + feedback capture checklist for accounts that show renewal risk. short, shareable with customer-facing teams.
Jorge Alvarez: love it. paste it here so SAs can grab copy/paste.
Maya Chen: sure — here's the customer-facing checklist (aimed at low-touch + bursty usage). feel free to edit language:```1) Health snapshot: share last 7d avg latency, token burn, and error rate. call out recent spikes and whether cache was warm.
2) Warmup plan: enable client-side prefill for top 3 user prompts (specify examples). suggest 1-2k prefix tokens to hydrate KV.
3) Batching guidance: set user-level concurrency to N and server-side batch window to 50–100ms for interactive loads.
4) Streaming fallback: if streaming gaps > 200ms, default to non-streaming fallback to avoid partial UX.
5) Telemetry hooks: require these events — request.id, model.variant, cache.hit=true/false, latency_ms, tokens_out.
6) Quick rollback: pin to previous model variant + disable quantization in case of quality regressions.
7) Renewal signal capture: ask customer 3 quick questions in product/email after go-live: usefulness (1–5), regressions noticed, feature ask.```
Priya Shah: two small additions — add the exact telemetry event names we use and a short template for the 3 post-go-live questions. also recommend a 24–72h warm-pool window after any bursty campaign.
Amir Patel: +1. sample prefill curl for engineering teams (keeps requests warm):```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"x-large-opti","input":"<top_prompt_example>","prefill":true,"prefill_tokens":1500}'
```Note: use small concurrency (2–4) to avoid spiking quota.
Maya Chen: nice — Priya can you drop the telemetry event names & the 3-question template? I'll make a one-pager for CS playbooks.
Priya Shah: here you go — telemetry: `cs.request_id`, `cs.model_variant`, `cs.cache_hit`, `cs.latency_ms`, `cs.tokens_out`, `cs.stream_gap_ms`. post-go-live template: 1) How helpful was the assistant today? (1–5) 2) Did you notice any drops in relevance or accuracy? (yes/no + comment) 3) What one feature would make this more valuable? (open)
Jorge Alvarez: wording tweak for the customer note: change "disable quantization" to "revert to full-precision variant" — less scary.
Maya Chen: updated locally. next steps: I will publish to the CS runbook repo and create a short email snippet SAs can copy. tagging @Jorge for review and @Amir for the prefill snippet.
CS Bot: reminder — add new runbook entry to repo: /repos/cs/runbooks/prefill-batch-stream.md. auto-label: "prefill-checklist".
Amir Patel: one more tactical: include a tiny observability assertion customers can run to verify cache warming:```python
# run this after prefill finishes
resp = client.get_metrics(query="cache_hit_rate{env='prod'}[1h]")
assert resp.p90 > 0.6
```This prevents false-positives in handoffs.
Maya Chen: perfect. i'll publish and ping #account-health with the tl;dr and a link to the full runbook. thanks all :pray: 
Jorge Alvarez: thanks — will slot in into next week's renewal-risk cadence deck.
Priya Shah: added to my enablement checklist too.
